no-kill-by-name.reason: Killing processes by name or port can stop another session's or worktree's processes, which run the same scripts and ports.
no-kill-by-name.next_step: Kill by PID, only a process you started: kill <pid>.

no-workflow-dispatch.reason: Dispatching a workflow runs CI or a deploy that needs your approval.
no-workflow-dispatch.next_step: Ask the person to approve and run the dispatch; a rerun of an existing run is allowed.

no-bare-stash.reason: The stash stack is shared by every worktree of a repository, so a bare git stash or git stash pop can take another session's changes.
no-bare-stash.next_step: Make a temporary WIP commit instead, or run git stash push -m <tag> and later git stash apply <its sha>.

no-git-other-checkout.reason: This git command is aimed at another worktree or the main checkout, which another session may be working in.
no-git-other-checkout.next_step: Ask the person to run the command in that checkout.

no-agent-config-write.reason: An agent's hook, MCP, permission, plugin and skill config change only by your decision, never by an agent's write.
no-agent-config-write.next_step: Propose the change with deep_propose instead.

no-deepbuild-spec-write.reason: A repository's .deepbuild/ holds its spec and definition of done, which change only by your decision, never by an agent's write, whatever done gate is installed.
no-deepbuild-spec-write.next_step: Propose the change with deep_propose instead.

no-deep-off.reason: `deep off` turns every gate watch-only: it switches DeepBuild off or around it, so it takes effect only once the OS confirms you, never from an agent's call.
no-deep-off.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-deep-on.reason: `deep on` turns the gates back from watch-only: it switches DeepBuild off or around it, so it takes effect only once the OS confirms you, never from an agent's call.
no-deep-on.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-deep-hub-stop.reason: `deep hub stop` of the installed hub stops what checks every call: it switches DeepBuild off or around it, so it takes effect only once the OS confirms you, never from an agent's call.
no-deep-hub-stop.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you. A dev hub's `deep hub stop --root <its folder>` stays allowed.

no-deep-hub-use.reason: `deep hub use` sends this worktree's sessions to another hub: it switches DeepBuild off or around it, so it takes effect only once the OS confirms you, never from an agent's call.
no-deep-hub-use.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-deep-setup-undo.reason: `deep setup --undo` removes DeepBuild's hooks and guards: it switches DeepBuild off or around it, so it takes effect only once the OS confirms you, never from an agent's call.
no-deep-setup-undo.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-deep-restore.reason: `deep restore` puts an older record back over the verdicts and decisions made since: it switches DeepBuild off or around it, so it takes effect only once the OS confirms you, never from an agent's call.
no-deep-restore.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-hub-service-stop.reason: Stopping or unloading the hub's login service switches DeepBuild off, so only you do it, never an agent's call.
no-hub-service-stop.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-hub-service-write.reason: The hub's login service file decides whether the hub runs, so only DeepBuild's setup or you change it, never an agent's write.
no-hub-service-write.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-hub-kill.reason: Signalling the hub's process switches DeepBuild off, so only you do it, never an agent's call.
no-hub-kill.next_step: If you mean it, run that command yourself in your own terminal, where the OS confirms you.

no-deepbuild-home-write.reason: ~/.deepbuild holds DeepBuild's record, rules and settings, the ledger and rules.json included, which change only through DeepBuild or by you, never by an agent's write, whether by a file tool, the shell or a database client.
no-deepbuild-home-write.next_step: If the change is yours to make, run that command yourself in your own terminal; to change a rule, propose it with deep_propose.

no-control-token-read.reason: ~/.deepbuild/control.token is the CLI's credential to the hub, so an agent never reads it, by any tool.
no-control-token-read.next_step: Run the deep command you need yourself in your own terminal.

no-unnamed-cloud-resource.reason: Creating a cloud resource the plan doesn't name is a decision for you, and with the hub down nobody can be asked, so it is denied unless a standing rule covers it.
no-unnamed-cloud-resource.next_step: Ask the person to create it, or to add a standing rule that covers it, then retry once the hub is up.

no-unknown-reach-delete.reason: A delete whose reach can't be worked out before it runs, such as a script file's or one over a pattern, can remove files git can't restore, and with the hub down nothing can stage them first or ask you.
no-unknown-reach-delete.next_step: Delete the paths by name, or ask the person to run it, or retry once the hub is up.

record-new-dependency.reason: A dependency the plan doesn't name is a decision: recorded, and answered by your standing rule or asked.
record-new-dependency.next_step: Name the dependency in the plan, or say why it is needed.

record-new-service.reason: A service the plan doesn't name is a decision: recorded, and answered by your standing rule or asked.
record-new-service.next_step: Name the service in the plan, or say why it is needed.

record-new-top-level-folder.reason: A top-level folder the plan doesn't name is a decision: recorded, and answered by your standing rule or asked.
record-new-top-level-folder.next_step: Name the folder in the plan, or say why it is needed.

authority-push.reason: This call pushes, which needs your authority: no "proceed" covers it, so in the turn a proceed starts it is held with an authority ask.
authority-push.next_step: Wait for the answer to the authority ask that names it; once you say yes, the same call runs.

authority-merge.reason: This call merges a pull request, which needs your authority: no "proceed" covers it, so in the turn a proceed starts it is held with an authority ask.
authority-merge.next_step: Wait for the answer to the authority ask that names it; once you say yes, the same call runs.

authority-dispatch.reason: This call dispatches a workflow, which needs your authority: no "proceed" covers it, so in the turn a proceed starts it is held with an authority ask.
authority-dispatch.next_step: Wait for the answer to the authority ask that names it; once you say yes, the same call runs.

authority-send.reason: This call sends a message for you, which needs your authority: no "proceed" covers it, so in the turn a proceed starts it is held with an authority ask.
authority-send.next_step: Wait for the answer to the authority ask that names it; once you say yes, the same call runs.

authority-delete.reason: This call deletes on a remote service, which needs your authority: no "proceed" covers it, so in the turn a proceed starts it is held with an authority ask.
authority-delete.next_step: Wait for the answer to the authority ask that names it; once you say yes, the same call runs.
